chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): We were in al-Bayda' at the end of the night, so I performed wudu and istaka (dried myself with dust), and I was about to pray. Then something entered my mind, so I asked: Is it permissible to pray in al-Bayda' while on the mount? He said: 'Do not pray in al-Bayda'.' I said: And where is the boundary of al-Bayda'? He said: 'Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), when he reached Dhat al-Jaysh, would hasten in his journey and would not pray until he reached the camp of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). I said to him: And where is Dhat al-Jaysh? He said: 'Three miles before al-Hafira'.

key_terms.الْبَيْدَاء: The open desert or wilderness, specifically a location on the route to Mecca
key_terms.الْحَفِيرَةِ: Al-Hafira, a well or station near Mecca
key_terms.اِسْتَكْتُ: I dried myself (with dust) after wudu
key_terms.ذَاتُ الْجَيْش: A specific location/station on the road to Mecca
key_terms.مُعَرَّسَ النَّبِيِّ: The camp of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)

ai.seo_question: Where is the boundary of al-Bayda' and where should one pray when traveling through it?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between the open desert (*al-Bayda'*) and established settlements (*al-Mu'arras*) for the validity of prayer during travel. By linking the boundary to the historical camp of Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) at *Dhat al-Jaysh*, it grounds the legal definition in the lived experience of the Ahl al-Bayt, emphasizing that prayer should be performed in recognized, settled areas rather than the barren wilderness.
